newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Traders see slight drop in Ukraine T-bill yields.
newsitem.headline: Traders see slight drop in Ukraine T-bill yields.

text.p: A slow decline in Ukraine Treasury bills, hovering between 20 and 30 percent for six- to 18-month paper, has been part of a government attempt to make its first foreign bonds more attractive, traders said on Monday.

First Ukrainian International Bank's Serhiy Monokha said the Finance Ministry and central bank were reducing T-bill yields to switch interest to foreign bonds, which Ukraine has said it will launch in September.
"Yields on Eurobonds would not be very big and T-bills with high yields would be better," Monokha said.
"If they decrease yields, it would make the Eurobond more interesting to foreigners."
Ukraine has announced the debut launch of dollar-denominated Eurobonds in September or October, to be preceded by a Samurai bond on Japanese markets.

Monokha said the ministry had also lowered issue volumes for Tuesday auctions. A central bank statement put six-month volumes at 12.6 million hryvnias, nine-month volumes at 11 million hryvnias, 12-month volumes at 22.6 million hryvnias, and 18-month volumes at 6.8 million hryvnias.
"There will be a decrease in yields, as usual," Monokha said.
"I don't know why there are such small volumes for 18-month bills," he added.

Six-month bills eased to 20.03 from 20.05 percent, nine-month bills slipped to 26.61 from 26.98 percent, 12-month bills to 26.61 from 26.98 percent and 18-month bills to 31.97 from 32.17 percent at auctions last week.
Alfa Capital analyst Erik Naiman predicted a further increase in demand for Ukrainian T-bills, especially from foreign buyers diverted by falling yields in neighbouring Russia.
"Yields on Russian GKOs have dropped so much in the last few months that they have significantly distanced themselves from yields on Ukrainian OVDPs," he said in a statement.
Naiman also forecast that yields in Ukrainian paper would continue to fall in the near future.
